correctness.rationale: The boundary-wire center has barycentric weights (b+c,a+c,a+b)/(2P). For a one-vertex arc the constraint X/u+Y/v=1 gives a strictly convex intercept sum; comparing its critical point against side endpoints yields the two exact branches. The fixed-perimeter side-pair monotonicity proves the longest-opposite vertex globally minimizes. The endpoint branch exceeds 1/3 by a<b+c; the interior branch exceeds 1/3 by a decreasing-in-a comparison and an exact feasibility polynomial factorization. The 1-1-epsilon family proves sharp unattained infimum. A standalone checker passed 6000 fixed-seed triangle tests and nine independent line-intersection tests; finite tests do not prove the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The Spieker center is the natural centroid for precisely the boundary-arclength measure under study. Identifying it as a canonical uniform one-third centerpoint, with a sharp two-branch exact depth across every triangle and an unattained extremal shape, answers a motivated geometric comparison to the published area-centroid 3/10 theorem. It is not merely a normalization check, an arbitrary slice, or a known-table recomputation.
